messages:
Alice Park: Quick sync — discovered a gap in how we log requests when the router triggers a fallback model. Right now we persist the original request + fallback path; that can leak PII. Need a short proposal: sampling + redaction ordering, console UX for debug opt-ins, and retention. cc @Ben Moore @Cara Liu
Ben Moore: Agreed. Current sampler runs at the edge before redaction to keep CPU low. If we flip to redaction -> sampling we get privacy but higher cost. Tradeoff. :thinking_face:
Cara Liu: What if we do deterministic sampling based on a salted hash of customer_id/request_id, then only run full redaction for sampled traces? Keeps volume small but lets us debug. Also add rule to scrub emails/names before any storage.
Dmitri Ivanov: Correlation risk: if we keep customer_id (even hashed) + routes, attackers could link events. Suggest we store only a peppered hash (server-side KMS pepper) and rotate pepper periodically. Store mapping in ephemeral vault for live debug only.
Emma Chen: Console UX: expose an org-level "debug log window" toggle. When enabled it requires two approvals and a justification. Display explicit PII risk banner and an automatic expiry (e.g., 72h). Also surface who enabled it in audit logs.
Frank Gomez: Perf note: the expensive part is regex/redaction on long prompt fields. Two-tier flow: cheap pre-sample (fast hash on request_id) -> if sampled then full redaction + enrichment + persist. Non-sampled: persist only metadata (trace_id, route, model, redaction_summary). That avoids redacting everything. :gear:
telemetry-bot: deploy-bot: log-sampler-v2 canary rolled to 10% of edge nodes (tag: canary/log-sampler-v2) — watch logs for error spikes.
Ben Moore: Also we should never log raw prompt text for Hosted by default. For Dedicated customers with opt-in we can allow more detailed logs but require KMS-backed access control and per-org retention overrides.
Alice Park: Retention proposals: redacted metadata -> 90d, sampled full redacted traces -> 30d, audit trails -> 365d. All at-rest encrypted with customer-specific KMS where available.
Cara Liu: Redaction rule examples (proposal): strip patterns for emails, phone numbers, credit card PANs; replace with <REDACTED:email> etc. Keep a redaction_summary field with counts of redactions but not the values.
Ben Moore: Example log snippet (for sampled traces):
```
{
  "trace_id": "tr_01Fxxx",
  "customer_hash": "hk_...",
  "route": "fallback->small-model",
  "redaction_summary": "email:1,phone:0",
  "prompt_redacted": "User asked about account <REDACTED:email>",
  "model": "gpt-small-v2",
  "timestamp": "1992001234"
}
```
Dmitri Ivanov: For hashing, use HMAC-SHA256(customer_id, KMS_pepper). Never log the raw customer_id. For debugging we can implement a secure unseal workflow that requires 2FA + audit event.
Emma Chen: Console: add a banner on query detail view when data was sampled vs only metadata. Also an indicator if privileged unseal was used.
Frank Gomez: Action: I'll run perf bench on doing redaction post-sample vs pre-sample. Expect ~2x CPU for full redaction path.
Ben Moore: I'll prototype sampler change (cheap-hash -> route) and feature flag it behind "sampler_two_tier".
Cara Liu: I'll update the redaction ruleset and write unit tests + some prompt-set coverage for edge PII cases.
Dmitri Ivanov: I'll mock KMS pepper rotate flow and write the key access audit checklist.
Emma Chen: I'll draft the console flows and approval UX, include the expiry and audit text.
Alice Park: Okay team — let's aim for a design doc by EOD Friday. Quick wins: Ben two-tier prototype + Frank perf numbers. Thanks. :thumbsup:
telemetry-bot: note: added metric `logsampler.sample_rate_edge` and `redaction.cpu_ms` to staging dashboards. Keep an eye on them.
Alice Park: thanks — we'll sync in 30m if anyone wants to join the deep dive.
